menu.welcome:
Welcome to Nuclear-Stic Mines.
Prepare to venture into the wasteland, survive its dangers, and "have fun"... after every death in this tactical, procedural roguelike strategy game inspired by Minesweeper.

phase1.dialog1: Hello, rescuer. Welcome to your training course, where you'll get ready to head out into the wasteland and rescue people.
phase1.dialog2: We'll start with the basics. Learn how to walk... You were supposed to have learned that years ago... whatever. Use the 'WASD' keys to move around.
phase1.dialog3: Good. Reach that marker ahead, and move carefully. Some things out there are a pain to get through, so it's usually best to go around them.

numbers.dialog1: Good. Now the part that actually keeps people alive out there: the numbers. Every revealed Tile shows how many Hazards are hiding in the 8 Tiles around it. Diagonals count.
numbers.dialog2: A 0 means every neighbor is safe. A 1 means exactly one of them is a Hazard. Hazards never show themselves, so you work it out.
numbers.dialog3: There's a Cactus somewhere in that crossing. Look at the numbers from different Tiles and find a lane that can't be hiding it.
numbers.dialog4: No flags for now. Just get to the goal without hugging anything spiky.
numbers.damageMessage: Ouch. That was the Cactus. Hazards cost you health, and you only have two points of it. Try again.
numbers.hint: Step next to the crossing and read the numbers. If two different Tiles both say 1, the Hazard must be among the neighbors they share.

phase2.dialog1: Great. You can read the numbers now, so let's put them to work. Below your icon you'll find a counter showing how many flags you have.
phase2.dialog2: You get exactly one flag per Hazard on the board. A flag marks a Tile you're sure is dangerous, so you don't step on it by accident.
phase2.dialog3: Use the arrow controls to place flags. They only work on hidden Tiles, the ones you can't see yet.
phase2.dialog4: Got it? Go mark that Hazard, then head for the goal.
phase2.damageMessage: Come on, it's not that hard, idiot. Running over to hug a cactus isn't exactly a good solution. Try again.
phase2.wrongFlagMessage: Do you have some kind of problem? Try again.
phase2.goalWithoutMarkingMessage: You haven't marked anything yet. Go place the flag...
phase2.successMessage: Well done. Now head for the goal.
phase2.hint: Flags only go on hidden Tiles. Stand next to where you think the Hazard is and press the arrow key toward it. Compare the neighboring numbers first.

phase3.dialog1: Now that you've mastered the art of flagging, you need to understand that Hazards are completely unpredictable.
phase3.dialog2: No one ever knows exactly where they are. If several of them are clustered in nearby Tiles, the Hazard Count will increase.
phase3.dialog3: You'll need to sharpen your deductive skills if you want to mark them or avoid them.
phase3.dialog4: Use all your flags and mark every one of them. You get exactly one flag per Hazard, so none are spare.
phase3.damageMessage: Read the damn numbers. Out in the wasteland, you'd be scattered across a hundred pieces by now.
phase3.wrongFlagMessage: Do you think flags grow on trees? Quit wasting them.
phase3.goalWithoutMarkingMessage: You haven't marked all the hazards yet. keep searching.
phase3.successMessage: All hazards marked! Well done. Now head for the goal.
phase3.hint: Count your flags: one per Hazard. If you've run out and Hazards remain, one of your flags is sitting on a safe Tile.

terrain.dialog1: Next lesson: the ground isn't flat. Every Tile has a height, and you can only climb one level at a time. Anything taller just stops you.
terrain.dialog2: Going down is easier, but not free. Drop one level and you're fine. Drop two or more and the fall costs you health.
terrain.dialog3: Get to the goal on the low ground. There's a staircase for the smart and a cliff for the rest. Your call.
terrain.damageMessage: That's what a cliff does to your legs. Stairs exist for a reason. I've patched you up, keep going.

phase4.dialog1: You can read the numbers and you can climb. Now let's put it all together: hills, Hazards and flags on the same course, just like out there.
phase4.dialog2: I've put this course together with different elevations. Remember: one level up at a time, and don't jump off ledges for fun.
phase4.dialog3: Mark the Hazards I've left up there, then make your way to the goal.
phase4.dialog4: By the way, I forgot to mention... there's an entity that keeps moving the hazards around. Only the ones you've marked stay put. You'll always have to plan new routes.
phase4.damageMessage: I'm not sure whether I should be worried about your mental state at this point.
phase4.wrongFlagMessage: Keep practicing. You're going to need it...
phase4.goalWithoutMarkingMessage: You still haven't marked them all. Keep looking.
phase4.successMessage: Fantastic. I'm proud of you. Head to the goal for the final challenge. I've got something special prepared.
phase4.hint: Hazards sit on the tallest Tiles of this course. Read the numbers around them and take the stairs.

phase5.dialog1: Your job out there is to find stranded children and bring them back to the starting point. Easy enough, right?
phase5.dialog2: For this final test, I want you to simulate a rescue. I've set up a dummy for you to retrieve and bring back. Good luck.
phase5.dialog3: Go find the dummy and bring it back to the start. And try not to kill yourself on the way.
phase5.damageMessage: If you bring back a child, I doubt they'll want to be rescued by someone with a strange obsession with hugging cacti. Please stop doing that.
phase5.successMessage: Good. Rescued, delivered, still in one piece. Don't get cocky, there's one more test.
phase5.manualPrompt: Oh, and by the way, I've got a manual that might actually keep you alive if you feel like reading it.
phase5.hint: Walk onto the dummy to pick it up, then bring it back to the Start Tile. Read the numbers so you don't step on a Cactus.

force.dialog1: Last exam, and it's a mean one. Two dummies this time, and you can only carry one at a time.
force.dialog2: When you're carrying all you can, your icon starts sweating. Bring that one back to the start, then go for the other.
force.dialog3: And remember the entity I mentioned? It only moves the Hazards you haven't marked. Watch what happens the moment you pick one up.
force.shuffle: See that? The Hazards you didn't mark moved. The ones you flagged stayed put. Every rescue reshuffles the rest, so don't trust your old notes. Read the numbers again.
force.damageMessage: Dead dummies are a hell of a bad look on your record. Try again, and read the numbers this time.
force.hint: Take one dummy back to the Start Tile before going for the other. After the first pickup the Hazards move, so re-read the numbers.
force.successMessage: That's everything I can teach you. Out there, you'll find plenty of things you won't see in this boring little training yard. Good luck...

tutorial.pitFall: HA! Watch where you're stepping. The ground out there is full of holes so deep that not even a vulture would bother going after your corpse. Try again.
tutorial.exhaustion: Heavy, isn't it? See those sweat drops on your icon? That means you're carrying as much as you can. Take this one back to the start first, then go back for the other.

infection.step1: Good day, esteemed sir. I regret to inform you that you have just devastated a property of considerable sentimental value to me. However, I am a reasonable individual and am willing to proceed through diplomatic channels.
infection.step2: Allow me to accompany you during your environmental sanitation labors. The presence of these deplorable Hazards constitutes an aesthetic affront that disturbs my usual contemplative walks.
infection.step3: With your permission, I shall temporarily adhere to your anatomy. I assure you this action has strictly professional purposes. You must mark {goal} hazards correctly to satisfy me.

success.main: Fascinating. Your performance has exceeded my statistical expectations. It is reassuring to verify that human incompetence is not a universal constant.
success.farewell: It has been a privilege to witness your activities. I hope not to encounter you again under catastrophic circumstances. Goodbye.

failure.main: Sir, I find myself deeply disappointed. The magnitude of this failure deserves a complete academic thesis. I shall express my discontent through slightly harmful means.
failure.damage: Consider this intervention a pedagogical correction and not a hostile act.

damage.main: What improper conduct! Attempting to murder an impartial observer constitutes a serious breach of civilized protocol.
damage.farewell: I have concluded that the preservation of my biological integrity has a higher priority than continuing this exchange. I wish you a moderately acceptable day.

horizon.name: Horizon
horizon.description: The earth reveals its secrets. They can be seen from the hidden.

home.name: Home
home.description: A beacon calls you back. You'll know how to get home.

topography.name: Topography
topography.description: The land remembers. You will keep your eyes on high.

memory.name: Memory
memory.description: Leave a mark on the world. Place up to 3 memories.

safekeeping.name: Safekeeping
safekeeping.description: Prevents wear and tear on some tools. And they don't get lost so easily.

revelation.name: Revelation
revelation.description: What is hidden will not remain so. Your hands will find the truth.

destiny.name: Destiny
destiny.description: Always points to who to save. The path is already written.

ascent.name: Ascent
ascent.description: Where others stumble, you climb. The summit is closer.

protection.name: Protection
protection.description: A scar that protects. The wounds that made you stronger.

descent.name: Descent
descent.description: The fall is not the end. You will survive the depths.

greed.name: Greed
greed.description: Gold calls. And you will know when it does.

salvation.name: Salvation
salvation.description: The abyss does not want you. You will escape.

stealth.name: Stealth
stealth.description: A velvet step. The world will not notice you.

purity.name: Purity
purity.description: Cleanse what others avoid. The stain will not be permanent.

concentration.name: Concentration
concentration.description: The prey reveals the terrain. Mark one and the land opens.

fortune.name: Fortune
fortune.description: The fool's luck. Fortune favors the bold.

vision.name: Vision
vision.description: What is seen is not forgotten. The eyes remember.

continuity.name: Continuity
continuity.description: The world has no end. What goes around comes around.

reversion.name: Reversion
reversion.description: Undo what was done. Time can bend.

stuffed.name: Stuffed
stuffed.description: What you carry will not be lost. Even in the end.

judgment.name: Judgment
judgment.description: The verdict is eternal. There is no appeal.

tips: A 0 means all eight neighbors are safe. Diagonals count, too.
You get exactly one flag per hazard. If you run out with hazards left, one of your flags is lying.
Flags only go on hidden tiles. Seen it already? Too late to flag it.
You can only climb one level at a time. Anything taller and you just stand there looking silly.
Dropping one level is free. Two or more, and your legs file a complaint.
Deliver pals by walking back onto the start tile. Yes, all the way back.
A sweaty icon means you can't carry any more pals. Drop them off first.
Every rescue shakes things up: hazards you didn't mark can move. Don't trust your old notes.
Marked hazards stay exactly where they are. That's the whole point of marking them.
Flags are free to place, but a wrong one will cost you. Be sure before you commit.
Chef can't take a flag back once it's placed. Aim well.
Mosquito, Mommy and Scout don't mark hazards automatically. Their flags stay flagged until they pick up a pal.
That's when the truth comes out: a flag on a hazard becomes marked. A flag on a safe tile gets you punished.
Every character carries a different number of pals at once. Know your limits before you go shopping for kids.
Heavier characters carry more pals per trip. Plan your route around it.
Some keychains unlock extra flag modes. Press F to cycle through them.
Keychains and bundles can change how a run plays out. Read their descriptions before you equip them.
Five keychain slots, five chances to make a questionable decision.
A bundle you didn't read is a bundle you didn't understand. Read it.
Reading the numbers from two different tiles tells you more than either one alone.
When in doubt, walk around. Detours are free. Cacti aren't.
Not sure what a number means? Open your diary. It's got answers and no judgment.
Cacti have no hard feelings about you. They just don't care.
The wasteland has no Wi-Fi. This loading screen is the closest you'll get to a signal.
Dying is a perfectly valid way to learn the map. Not recommended, though.
Pausing is allowed. The hazards will wait. They have nothing better to do.
Remember: the numbers never lie. The player does.
If it looks safe, check the numbers again. If it still looks safe, check them one more time.
Another day, another wasteland. Try to have fun... or whatever this is.
